quote: Prices are coming down, and some of the offsets being offered by the state are attractive.
stewart_read: Customer hands over a clean interest reason (price trend + state incentives) but Joel never reflects it back later to build forward pull.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the reason too generic to anchor on, favoring the bill number instead — but the bill number was also never flipped.
coaching_implication: Reflect the customer's stated reason back at button-up: 'so the specialist can walk you through exactly how those state offsets apply to your bill.'

quote: On the average, I'd say it's somewhere around $400.
stewart_read: Bill captured cleanly but treated as data point, not flipped into alignment-against-utility.
coaching_implication: Should have flipped: 'so you're basically handing Northern Neck $400+ a month no matter what — that's what we're trying to take back.'

quote: We go between 3 and 6 quite regularly.
stewart_read: A $200-300 swing month to month is a huge pain point and an enthusiasm signal for high-usage relief, but rep just calls it 'crazy' and moves on.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be strategically saving the number for the specialist's proposal rather than over-selling on the setter call.
coaching_implication: Even without selling, rep could verbally flag the range as exactly why an offset makes sense — sets up specialist's pitch.

stewart_read: Third distinct bill figure volunteered; rep never reconciles the numbers into one anchor for the pitch.
coaching_implication: Consolidate: 'so somewhere between $400 and $620 depending on season — that's the number we're designing against.'

quote: We we consume a lot of electricity.
stewart_read: Customer self-identifies as a high-usage household (dual 200-amp panel service), a strong qualifying signal for a larger system.
coaching_implication: Rep acknowledged but should have tied this explicitly to appointment value: 'that high usage is exactly why this design will show real savings.'

quote: Can you I'm I wanna put my wife on the cell on the speaker.
stewart_read: Customer self-initiates including his wife; rep's response ('My wife is the same way') was warm but didn't explicitly confirm her for the appointment itself.
coaching_implication: Should have explicitly locked her onto the appointment: 'great, let's get a time that works for both of you.'

quote: And is this a phone number that can receive a text message?
stewart_read: Button-up is missing the one-hour block statement, the no-driving/computer instruction, and the 'is that fair' handshake — verified events confirm only partial completion.
coaching_implication: Add the full button-up checklist verbally before ending the call to reduce no-show risk.
